desc: Read the input values for $N$, $M$, starting position $(S_x, S_y)$, house coordinates, and the sequence of moves $(D_i, C_i)$.
Initialize the current position $(curr\_x, curr\_y)$ to $(S_x, S_y)$ and an empty set `visited_houses` to store unique house coordinates encountered.
Update the current position based on the direction and distance.

If the move is horizontal (L/R), determine the range of x-coordinates covered. Check if any house has an x-coordinate within this range and a y-coordinate equal to the current y. If found, add the house to `visited_houses`.

If the move is vertical (U/D), determine the range of y-coordinates covered. Check if any house has a y-coordinate within this range and an x-coordinate equal to the current x. If found, add the house to `visited_houses`.
After processing all moves, output the final coordinates and the size of the `visited_houses` set.
Write the Python code implementing the described algorithm with DSU optimization for efficient distinct house counting.
Implement the iterative DSU `find` function to avoid recursion depth issues.
Handle the initialization of DSU structures lazily (only when a line is first accessed).
Verify boundary conditions for binary search and segment ranges.
